title: What is an hypothesis and how do you specify one?

cues.en: Mike: This section of the course is all about hypothesis testing.
cues.zh: Mike：這一章完全圍繞假設檢定。

cues.en: So I thought it would be a good idea to start with a lecture where I say what an hypothesis even is.
cues.zh: 所以先用一堂課，說明假設到底是什麼，應該很好。

cues.en: So in this video, you're going to learn what is an hypothesis?
cues.zh: 這部影片會學到，什麼是假設？

cues.en: What it means to be a good hypothesis versus a bad hypothesis.
cues.zh: 好的假設和不好的假設，有什麼意義。

cues.en: You'll see a bunch of examples of good and bad and not hypotheses.
cues.zh: 會看到很多好假設、壞假設，以及根本不是假設的例子。

cues.en: And I will also introduce this term called the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 也會介紹虛無假設這個詞。

cues.en: It's a bit of a weird term.
cues.zh: 這個詞有點奇怪。

cues.en: Let's start with a general definition.
cues.zh: 先從一般定義開始。

cues.en: So an hypothesis is a falsifiable claim that requires verification.
cues.zh: 假設是需要驗證、而且可以被否證的主張。

cues.en: And this verification comes from experimental or observational data.
cues.zh: 驗證來自實驗或觀察資料。

cues.en: And an hypothesis allows for predictions about future observations or future phenomenon.
cues.zh: 假設也能對未來觀察或未來現象做出預測。

cues.en: So quite a mouthful of a definition here, but this will make even more sense as I unpack it throughout the rest of this video, along with some examples.
cues.zh: 定義有點長，但隨著影片接下來逐步拆解、舉例，會更容易理解。

cues.en: So why are hypotheses important?
cues.zh: 為什麼假設重要？

cues.en: This is a course on statistics.
cues.zh: 這是統計課。

cues.en: It's not a course on hypotheses.
cues.zh: 不是假設課。

cues.en: Well, hypotheses improve experiment design, they improve your critical thinking, and relevant for this course, they improve data analyses.
cues.zh: 假設能改善實驗設計、增進批判思考，而且對這門課而言，也能改善資料分析。

cues.en: So it's very difficult to do data analyses, or that is to do good, meaningful, important data analyses without having clear hypotheses
cues.zh: 如果沒有明確假設，就很難進行資料分析，也就是做出良好、有意義、重要的資料分析，

cues.en: to anchor those analyses to.
cues.zh: 因為這些分析需要假設作為依據。

cues.en: And in part, that's because hypotheses allow you to transform your loose ideas, your speculations into concrete, specific claims that are testable.
cues.zh: 一部分原因是，假設能把鬆散的想法、推測，轉成具體、明確、可檢驗的主張。

cues.en: So hypotheses are used to develop new and more accurate theories, and hypotheses can be used to dissolve bad theories.
cues.zh: 假設可以用來發展更新、更準確的理論，也可以推翻不好的理論。

cues.en: This is important in science.
cues.zh: 這對科學很重要。

cues.en: Developing new theories in science is important, but getting rid of bad theories is equally important, maybe even more important.
cues.zh: 發展新理論很重要，但排除壞理論同樣重要，甚至更重要。

cues.en: And I think it's fair to claim that most progress in science, progress in engineering, progress in medicine, progress in technology,
cues.zh: 我認為可以合理地說，科學、工程、醫學和科技的大部分進步，

cues.en: it's all the result of hypothesis testing.
cues.zh: 都是假設檢定的結果。

cues.en: So you develop a strong hypothesis and you test it empirically, and that allows for the expansion and increase of knowledge.
cues.zh: 提出有力的假設，透過實證檢驗，就能拓展、增加知識。

cues.en: Okay, so what makes a strong hypothesis?
cues.zh: 那怎樣才是有力的假設？

cues.en: So a strong hypothesis is clear.
cues.zh: 有力的假設要清楚。

cues.en: It is specific.
cues.zh: 要具體。

cues.en: It is falsifiable.
cues.zh: 要可否證。

cues.en: That means that you can falsify. You can prove it wrong.
cues.zh: 表示可以否證，能證明它錯。

cues.en: A good hypothesis is based on prior data, or it's based on an existing theory.
cues.zh: 好的假設以先前資料或現有理論為基礎。

cues.en: A good hypothesis leads to a statistical test.
cues.zh: 好的假設能導向統計檢定。

cues.en: So there is a way to test that hypothesis.
cues.zh: 也就是有方法檢驗。

cues.en: It has to be a statement and not a question.
cues.zh: 必須是陳述，而不是問題。

cues.en: A good hypothesis is about a prediction about the direction of an effect, not just saying that something will be different from something else somehow, somewhere
cues.zh: 好的假設會預測效果的方向，而不只是說，宇宙某處、某個時間，某個東西會用某種方式，

cues.en: in the universe at some point in time.
cues.zh: 和另一個東西不同。

cues.en: So you should be specific about exactly what is going to happen with the experimental manipulation or whatever it is you are looking at.
cues.zh: 應該具體說明，實驗操弄或研究對象，究竟會發生什麼。

cues.en: A good hypothesis is also relevant for unobserved data.
cues.zh: 好的假設，也適用於尚未觀察的資料。

cues.en: So your hypothesis should be relevant for something that hasn't happened yet, or data that haven't been measured yet.
cues.zh: 應該對尚未發生的事情，或尚未量測的資料有意義。

cues.en: And of course, a good hypothesis is relevant for understanding nature.
cues.zh: 當然，也要有助於理解自然。

cues.en: It's somehow relevant to making things better, or it's relevant to understanding something better.
cues.zh: 和改善事物，或更深入理解事物，有某種關聯。

cues.en: It's somehow relevant to the world beyond one simple, stupid little dataset that you happen to be working with.
cues.zh: 要對當下這一小組簡單資料之外的世界，也有意義。

cues.en: Okay, so what I want to do now is go through a bunch of examples of not hypotheses, weak hypotheses, and strong hypotheses.
cues.zh: 接著看一系列不是假設、弱假設和強假設的例子。

cues.en: So here's our first example.
cues.zh: 第一個例子。

cues.en: Here is a statement. This is not an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這是一個陳述，不是假設。

cues.en: Medical research is important for curing diseases.
cues.zh: 醫學研究對治療疾病很重要。

cues.en: Now, this is a good statement.
cues.zh: 這是很好的陳述。

cues.en: I agree wholeheartedly, I would say.
cues.zh: 我完全同意。

cues.en: I would even go further and say, all governments in the world should be spending more money, we should be investing more money, more manpower
cues.zh: 甚至會進一步說，世界各國政府都應投入更多經費，我們應投入更多資金、人力，

cues.en: into medical research to better diagnose and treat and cure diseases.
cues.zh: 進行醫學研究，改善疾病診斷、治療和治癒。

cues.en: I agree 1,000,000% with this statement.
cues.zh: 我百分之一百萬同意。

cues.en: Nonetheless, it is not an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 但它不是假設。

cues.en: Nowhere even close to an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 連接近假設都談不上。

cues.en: Okay, here is an example of an hypothesis that is weak.
cues.zh: 這裡則是一個弱假設。

cues.en: It's not a good hypothesis, but it is still technically an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 不是好的假設，但技術上仍然是假設。

cues.en: So the medication has an effect.
cues.zh: 這種藥物有某種效果。

cues.en: Well, you know, okay, so we can try to falsify this claim, but it's not very clear, it's not very specific,
cues.zh: 好，可以試著否證這個主張，但不太清楚、不太具體，

cues.en: and it's not really relevant for understanding nature or medication or the disease or whatever.
cues.zh: 也不太有助於理解自然、藥物、疾病或其他相關內容。

cues.en: So for example, let's say you have some medication that helps you sleep at night, but then what it actually does
cues.zh: 例如，有一種幫助夜晚睡眠的藥，但實際上，

cues.en: is it turns your fingers black and then your hands fall off.
cues.zh: 它會讓手指變黑，然後手掌掉下來。

cues.en: God, that would be an awful thing to happen!
cues.zh: 天啊，那太可怕了！

cues.en: So the medication clearly has an effect.
cues.zh: 藥物顯然有效果。

cues.en: But the effect has nothing to do with what the medication is for.
cues.zh: 但效果和藥物用途無關。

cues.en: And it's an awful effect. So this is a weak hypothesis.
cues.zh: 而且很糟，所以這是弱假設。

cues.en: Here's a strong hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這裡是強假設。

cues.en: The medication reduces a particular symptom in a dose-response fashion.
cues.zh: 藥物以劑量反應的方式，減輕某個特定症狀。

cues.en: Dose-response fashion means that the more of the dose, that the more of the medication that you give, so the higher the dose, the more the symptom is relieved.
cues.zh: 劑量反應的意思，是給越多藥物、劑量越高，症狀就減輕越多。

cues.en: So that would be a dose-response fashion.
cues.zh: 這就是劑量反應。

cues.en: So this is a clear hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這是清楚的假設。

cues.en: It's specific. It's falsifiable.
cues.zh: 具體，而且可否證。

cues.en: It leads to a particular statistical test, in this case, probably an ANOVA or regression.
cues.zh: 能導向特定統計檢定，這個例子可能是 ANOVA 或迴歸。

cues.en: You'll learn about those later on in the course.
cues.zh: 課程後面會學到。

cues.en: And it makes predictions about unobserved data and so on.
cues.zh: 也能對尚未觀察的資料做預測等等。

cues.en: Okay, let's go through one more example.
cues.zh: 再看一個例子。

cues.en: So here's an example of something that is not an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這是另一個不是假設的例子。

cues.en: Will students pass this course?
cues.zh: 學生會通過這門課嗎？

cues.en: First of all, it's a question. It's not even a statement.
cues.zh: 首先，它是問題，連陳述都不是。

cues.en: Again, it's a very important question to ask.
cues.zh: 同樣，是非常重要的問題。

cues.en: We can think of generating hypotheses from this question, but this thing on its own is not an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 可以由此產生假設，但這句本身不是假設。

cues.en: Okay, and again, here I'm going to give you an example of a weak hypothesis.
cues.zh: 再給一個弱假設例子。

cues.en: It's not a very good hypothesis, but it is still one.
cues.zh: 不是很好，但仍然是假設。

cues.en: Studying improves grades.
cues.zh: 讀書能改善成績。

cues.en: Now, I certainly hope that that's true.
cues.zh: 我當然希望是真的。

cues.en: Obviously, this is true in nearly all cases, but it's not very specific and it's kind of hard to contextualize this.
cues.zh: 顯然幾乎所有情況都是真的，但不太具體，也很難放進明確情境。

cues.en: So here is a stronger hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這裡是更強的假設。

cues.en: A combination of self-study and group study will improve final exam grades by at least 10%.
cues.zh: 結合自學與團體學習，能讓期末考成績提升至少 10%。

cues.en: So this is much better.
cues.zh: 這就好多了。

cues.en: It's very clear and specific on multiple fronts.
cues.zh: 在多個面向都很清楚、具體。

cues.en: It's clear about the types of study.
cues.zh: 清楚指出學習類型。

cues.en: So this hypothesis says two different kinds of study.
cues.zh: 這個假設提到兩種不同學習方式。

cues.en: And it's also clear on the outcome.
cues.zh: 對結果也很清楚。

cues.en: The outcome is improving final exam grades, so not just grades in general, but final exam grades by at least 10%.
cues.zh: 結果是提升期末考成績，不是籠統的成績，而且至少提升 10%。

cues.en: Really, really specific.
cues.zh: 非常具體。

cues.en: And what I also like about this hypothesis is that it's inspiring.
cues.zh: 也喜歡它具有啟發性。

cues.en: It leads you to think more about better research in the future.
cues.zh: 讓你思考未來更好的研究。

cues.en: Additional tests that you can run.
cues.zh: 還能進行哪些額外檢驗。

cues.en: You know, what is the optimal balance of self-study and group study?
cues.zh: 例如，自學與團體學習的最佳平衡是什麼？

cues.en: And does it depend on the type of exam?
cues.zh: 是否取決於考試類型？

cues.en: All sorts of interesting questions you can think of based on this hypothesis.
cues.zh: 根據這個假設，可以想到各種有趣問題。

cues.en: All right, so now it's your turn.
cues.zh: 現在輪到你。

cues.en: What I have here is a list of seven points.
cues.zh: 這裡列出七點。

cues.en: And what I want you to do in a moment is pause the video and go through these and label each of these seven points as one of three options.
cues.zh: 等一下請暫停影片，逐一檢視，將每一點標記為三種選項之一。

cues.en: You can label it as not an hypothesis, a weak hypothesis, or a strong hypothesis.
cues.zh: 不是假設、弱假設，或強假設。

cues.en: Okay, so now you get to pause the video.
cues.zh: 現在可以暫停影片。

cues.en: How did it go? Did you do it?
cues.zh: 結果如何？有做嗎？

cues.en: Were you satisfied?
cues.zh: 滿意嗎？

cues.en: Were any of these particularly challenging to decide?
cues.zh: 有沒有哪一個特別難判斷？

cues.en: Well, now I'm gonna go through my answers.
cues.zh: 現在說明我的答案。

cues.en: So statement one is, there are other universes with different physical rules.
cues.zh: 第一句，有其他宇宙，其物理法則不同。

cues.en: That is a super interesting thing to think about.
cues.zh: 非常有趣，值得思考。

cues.en: Totally mind-boggling to consider this possibility.
cues.zh: 考慮這種可能性，真的令人驚嘆。

cues.en: However, it is not an hypothesis, and that's because it's not falsifiable.
cues.zh: 但不是假設，因為不可否證。

cues.en: We can't do an experiment.
cues.zh: 無法做實驗。

cues.en: We can't collect data and provide support for or against this statement.
cues.zh: 無法收集資料，提供支持或反對這句話的證據。

cues.en: So again, really thought-provoking statement.
cues.zh: 再次說明，非常引人思考。

cues.en: Not an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 但不是假設。

cues.en: Here we go. Wearing purple underwear improves mood.
cues.zh: 接著，穿紫色內褲能改善心情。

cues.en: I have no idea if that's the case, but it's a strong hypothesis.
cues.zh: 不知道是否如此，但這是強假設。

cues.en: It's clear. It's specific.
cues.zh: 清楚、具體。

cues.en: It's falsifiable.
cues.zh: 可否證。

cues.en: It can make predictions about unobserved data points.
cues.zh: 能對尚未觀察的資料點做預測。

cues.en: A bit of a silly hypothesis, but it's still a strong hypothesis.
cues.zh: 有點傻，但仍是強假設。

cues.en: Plants grow differently in sugar water.
cues.zh: 植物在糖水中生長得不同。

cues.en: Again, that is a valid hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這是有效的假設。

cues.en: There is something to falsify.
cues.zh: 有可以否證的內容。

cues.en: We can get evidence for or against this, but it's not a really great one because we don't say what differently means.
cues.zh: 能取得支持或反對的證據，但不太好，因為沒有說「不同」是什麼意思。

cues.en: Are these plants growing better or worse in sugar water?
cues.zh: 在糖水中，植物長得更好還是更差？

cues.en: Are they gonna start growing horizontally instead of vertically?
cues.zh: 會開始橫著長，而不是向上長嗎？

cues.en: So this could be improved to be a strong hypothesis.
cues.zh: 所以可以改善成強假設。

cues.en: Okay, Mike X Cohen's courses are awesome.
cues.zh: 好，Mike X Cohen 的課程很棒。

cues.en: Well, I certainly hope you agree with this statement, but it is definitely not an hypothesis, unfortunately.
cues.zh: 當然希望你同意，但可惜，這肯定不是假設。

cues.en: Okay, washing hands for 20 seconds reduces disease spread.
cues.zh: 洗手 20 秒能減少疾病傳播。

cues.en: A very strong hypothesis.
cues.zh: 非常有力的假設。

cues.en: It's clear. It's falsifiable.
cues.zh: 清楚、可否證。

cues.en: It's specific. We can test various things.
cues.zh: 具體，可以檢驗各種事情。

cues.en: Is it 15 seconds?
cues.zh: 15 秒呢？

cues.en: Is that also enough? And so on.
cues.zh: 是否也足夠？等等。

cues.en: Number six, an apple a day keeps the doctor away.
cues.zh: 第六，一天一蘋果，醫生遠離我。

cues.en: This is a famous expression.
cues.zh: 這是著名諺語。

cues.en: I doubt that it's really, actually true.
cues.zh: 我懷疑真的完全如此。

cues.en: It's a fairly weak hypothesis.
cues.zh: 是相當弱的假設。

cues.en: What does it mean to keep the doctor away?
cues.zh: 讓醫生遠離是什麼意思？

cues.en: Presumably, it means that eating an apple every day keeps you healthy.
cues.zh: 大概表示每天吃蘋果能保持健康。

cues.en: But yeah, I don't know.
cues.zh: 但我不知道。

cues.en: This could be improved quite a bit.
cues.zh: 這可以改善很多。

cues.en: Okay, and then this last one, well, this is just a question.
cues.zh: 最後這個，只是一個問題。

cues.en: It's not even a statement.
cues.zh: 連陳述都不是。

cues.en: It's certainly not a hypothesis.
cues.zh: 肯定不是假設。

cues.en: But you could come up with an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 但可以想出一個假設。

cues.en: You could even develop a strong hypothesis based on this question.
cues.zh: 甚至可以根據問題，提出強假設。

cues.en: But this question, on its own, is not an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 但問題本身不是假設。

cues.en: An example of this could be, you know, people score higher on a test of creative problem solving
cues.zh: 例如，人們在創意問題解決測驗上的得分，會在

cues.en: after watching 15 minutes of stand-up comedy.
cues.zh: 看過 15 分鐘單口喜劇之後提高。

cues.en: So that would be an example of a strong hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這就是強假設的例子。

cues.en: But this thing on its own is a question.
cues.zh: 但這句本身是問題。

cues.en: It's not an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 不是假設。

cues.en: Okay, so I hope that makes sense.
cues.zh: 希望這樣說清楚了。

cues.en: You will see lots more examples of hypotheses throughout this course.
cues.zh: 課程中會看到更多假設例子。

cues.en: I now need to tell you about something called the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 現在需要介紹所謂虛無假設。

cues.en: So the null hypothesis is like the boring hypothesis.
cues.zh: 虛無假設就像無聊的假設。

cues.en: It's the hypothesis that nothing interesting is happening in the data.
cues.zh: 假設資料裡沒有發生有趣的事。

cues.en: It's the hypothesis that your manipulation had no effect on the data.
cues.zh: 假設你的操弄對資料沒有影響。

cues.en: So it's a little bit counterintuitive because when you're designing research, when you're doing an experiment or looking at existing data, what you actually specify
cues.zh: 這有一點反直覺，因為設計研究、進行實驗或查看既有資料時，實際指定的，

cues.en: is called the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 稱為對立假設。

cues.en: Now, in my opinion, this is a little bit of an aside, but in my opinion, we shouldn't be calling this the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 我個人認為，這稍微岔題一下，我覺得不該叫對立假設。

cues.en: We should be calling it the effect hypothesis, because the hypothesis is that there is an effect.
cues.zh: 應該叫效果假設，因為假設的是存在效果。

cues.en: It's not an hypothesis that there is an alternative.
cues.zh: 不是假設存在某種替代方案。

cues.en: But anyway, you know, sometimes these terms get introduced into the literature many, many decades ago by non-native English speakers.
cues.zh: 但有時術語是好幾十年前，由非英語母語者引入文獻，

cues.en: And then they just end up stuck in the literature.
cues.zh: 後來就固定在文獻裡。

cues.en: And that's the term that we all use.
cues.zh: 變成大家都使用的名稱。

cues.en: Okay, nonetheless. End bracket.
cues.zh: 好，岔題到此結束。

cues.en: So when you're doing research, you actually specify the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 做研究時，實際指定的是對立假設。

cues.en: That's what guides your research.
cues.zh: 它引導研究方向。

cues.en: But in statistical analyses, you don't actually test the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 但統計分析中，實際上不檢驗對立假設。

cues.en: You're always testing the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 總是檢驗虛無假設。

cues.en: And then the question is, do your data support the null hypothesis or not?
cues.zh: 問題是，資料是否支持虛無假設？

cues.en: And then what you hope to find is that the data do not support the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 希望發現資料不支持虛無假設。

cues.en: So you reject the null hypothesis in favor of the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 因此拒絕虛無假設，轉而傾向對立假設。

cues.en: So it's a little weird, it's a little counterintuitive that research is all about the interesting hypotheses, but statistics, inferential statistics are actually
cues.zh: 這有點奇怪、反直覺，研究關心的是有趣的假設，但統計、推論統計其實

cues.en: all about the boring, plain, vanilla null hypotheses.
cues.zh: 關心無聊、平凡、普通的虛無假設。

cues.en: Okay, and the null hypotheses are often shorthand written as H nought.
cues.zh: 虛無假設經常簡寫為 H₀。

cues.en: This is pronounced H nought.
cues.zh: 發音是 H nought。

cues.en: It's not not like N-O-T.
cues.zh: 不是 not，不是 N-O-T。

cues.en: It's nought, the old English word for zero, which is nought.
cues.zh: 而是 nought，古英語中表示 0 的字。

cues.en: So H with a zero in the subscript, or sometimes it's just a full-size zero.
cues.zh: 也就是 H 加上下標 0，有時也用一般大小的 0。

cues.en: So H0 is called H nought.
cues.zh: 所以 H0 唸作 H nought。

cues.en: It's also called the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 也稱虛無假設。

cues.en: Okay. So here's an example of the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這裡是虛無假設的例子。

cues.en: So we start with our alternative hypothesis, HA, and that is that people will buy more widgets after seeing advertisement X compared to advertisement Y.
cues.zh: 先從對立假設 Hₐ 開始：相較於廣告 Y，人們看過廣告 X 後，會買更多小商品。

cues.en: So this is some marketing company or a business, and they're testing out different kinds of advertisements.
cues.zh: 某家行銷公司或企業，測試不同廣告。

cues.en: So people buy more widgets after ad X compared to ad Y.
cues.zh: 看過 X 廣告後，人們比看過 Y 廣告買更多小商品。

cues.en: So then we have the null hypothesis, and that is that the advertisement type has no effect on widget purchases.
cues.zh: 虛無假設則是，廣告類型對商品購買沒有影響。

cues.en: In other words, that people buy the same number of widgets regardless of which advertisement type they see.
cues.zh: 換句話說，不管看哪種廣告，購買數量都相同。

cues.en: So again, this is how you set up your research.
cues.zh: 這就是研究的設定方式。

cues.en: This is the thing you're interested in.
cues.zh: 這是感興趣的內容。

cues.en: And in your statistical analyses, as you will learn over the next videos, and for the rest of this course, what you're actually doing is gathering evidence,
cues.zh: 接下來幾部影片，以及本課剩餘內容會學到，統計分析實際上是在收集證據，

cues.en: determining the strength of the evidence for the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 判斷支持虛無假設的證據有多強。

cues.en: And if the evidence for the null hypothesis is really weak, so the data don't actually support the null hypothesis, then you say, well, we reject the null hypothesis
cues.zh: 如果支持虛無假設的證據很弱，也就是資料不支持虛無假設，就會說，拒絕虛無假設，

cues.en: and we tentatively favor the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 暫時傾向對立假設。

cues.en: And the reason why we set it up like that is because it's not actually possible to prove an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這樣設定，是因為其實無法證明假設為真。

cues.en: In science, you cannot prove an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 在科學中，不能證明一個假設。

cues.en: All you can do is reject an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 只能拒絕假設。

cues.en: So you can disprove an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 可以證明它錯。

cues.en: Or you can fail to reject an hypothesis.
cues.zh: 或者無法拒絕假設。

cues.en: And if you fail to reject the hypothesis, that's interpreted as the hypothesis being tentatively supported, at least until a better hypothesis comes around.
cues.zh: 如果無法拒絕，就解讀為暫時支持，至少直到有更好的假設出現。

cues.en: Okay, so in this video, you learned about hypotheses, definitions of hypotheses, the distinction between not an hypothesis, a weak hypothesis, and a strong hypothesis,
cues.zh: 這部影片學到假設及其定義，以及不是假設、弱假設和強假設的區別。

cues.en: I told you about the characteristics of a strong hypothesis, and we saw lots of examples of good and bad hypotheses.
cues.zh: 也介紹強假設的特徵，並看了很多好、壞假設的例子。
